hero.lead: A nation of 18.9 million at Africa’s western edge, with a $2.2 billion IMF programme agreed by staff and World Bank finance for its water, roads, health care and buses.

capital.heading: Senegal is resetting its finances in the open. Next, safe water in every home.

record.text: IMF Extended Credit Facility agreed at staff level on 1 September 2026, 36 months; subject to Executive Board approval
Total public sector debt at end-2024, FCFA 25,583 billion: central government 119.0% and the parapublic sector 9.6% of GDP, before the rebasing of GDP
record.source: Ministry of Economy, Finance and Plan, 2026

record.text: Three World Bank financing agreements signed on 5 August 2026: emergency response, roads in farming areas, and Casamance and eastern Senegal
record.source: Ministry of Economy, Finance and Plan, 2026

record.text: Water security and sanitation, first phase of an $800 million programme, with sanitation for about 600,000 people in greater Dakar
Health system and financial protection, paid on results, for women, children and vulnerable families

register.name: Second public bond offering of 2026
register.detail: Results announced 14 October 2026 · public offering (appel public à l’épargne) in CFA francs · target FCFA 200 billion
register.text: The second public bond offering of the year, sold to savers and investors in CFA francs. It raised far more than its target, and debt in CFA francs stays outside the scope of the debt treatment plan announced on 1 September 2026.
by: Ministry of Economy, Finance and Plan

register.name: First public bond offering of 2026
register.detail: Subscriptions 26 February to 26 March 2026 · 3, 5, 7 and 10 years at 6.40%, 6.60%, 6.75% and 6.95% · target FCFA 200 billion
register.text: The first public bond offering of 2026 (appel public à l’épargne), in four maturities from three to ten years. Its proceeds help finance the 2026 budget, which pays for the schools, clinics and water services behind the seven standards.
by: Ministry of Economy, Finance and Plan

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: Staff-level agreement 1 September 2026 · 36 months · SDR 1,537.1 million, 475% of quota · subject to IMF Executive Board approval
register.note: Board approval requires corrective actions on past misreporting and financing assurances from partners
register.text: Commits Senegal to raise domestic revenue, with a medium-term revenue strategy in 2027, to control spending while raising social outlays such as targeted cash transfers, and to strengthen debt management and the oversight of state enterprises. Before the Board decides, Senegal must take corrective actions on past misreporting and receive financing assurances from its partners.

register.name: Enhancing Connectivity in the Northern and Central Agricultural Production Areas, second additional financing
register.detail: Approved July 2026 · EUR 119.6 million from IDA · signed 5 August 2026 · project total $470.8 million
register.note: 171 km of paved roads and 104 km of laterite tracks
register.text: Adds two road corridors to a project that has already built or upgraded 414 km of roads in farming regions. About 570,000 people benefit directly, including 221,000 along the new corridors, with easier access to markets and services.

register.name: Casamance Economic Development Project, additional financing
register.detail: Approved, announced 29 June 2026 · IDA · signed 5 August 2026 · project total $85 million
register.text: Additional finance for economic development in Casamance and Kédougou, two regions in the south and east of the country. About 850,000 people are to benefit from better services and income.

register.name: Health System Development and Financial Protection Program (NAATANGUE 2030)
register.detail: Approved, announced 18 March 2026 · $100 million IDA credit, $20 million GFF grant, $15 million HSTRF grant · results-based
register.note: Care for mothers and newborns, health insurance for vulnerable groups, essential medicines
register.text: Expands emergency obstetric and newborn care, routine screening for women and children, effective health insurance for vulnerable groups and the supply of essential medicines, and sends health workers to underserved areas. It pays on results, which ties the money to the health standard.
by: Health System Transformation and Resilience Multi-Donor Trust Fund

register.name: Strengthening Senegal’s Fiscal Sustainability Program (SEN-FISCALE)
register.detail: Approved, announced 24 June 2025 · IDA · $105 million Program-for-Results and $10 million of technical assistance
register.note: Debt sustainability, public financial management and domestic revenue
register.text: Supports the 2025–2029 reform programme for public finance: the sustainability of public debt, financial management and the revenue Senegal raises at home. Domestic revenue is what pays for the seven standards year after year.

register.name: Dakar Sustainable Urban Mobility Project
register.detail: Approved, announced 17 June 2025 · IDA · first phase of a wider programme
register.note: Bus rapid transit linked to the regional express train
register.text: Finances a bus rapid transit line linked to the regional express train, restructured bus networks and low-emission buses on priority corridors, and the move of informal transport workers into structured jobs. The World Bank expects it to unlock economic opportunities for 3.8 million people in the Dakar area.

register.name: Integrated Water Security and Sanitation Program (PISEA), phase 1
register.detail: Approved, announced 21 June 2024 · IDA · first phase of a ten-year, $800 million multiphase programme
register.note: Sanitation for about 600,000 people in greater Dakar
register.text: Builds sewers and a treatment plant in parts of Pikine and Guédiawaye, reduces water losses and improves the Lac de Guiers supply. More than seven million people are to benefit from better water management, on the standard that sets Senegal’s Coverage.

register.name: Green Climate Finance Facility for Fostering Climate-Smart Agriculture (FP262)
register.detail: Approved 20 February 2025 · USD 20.94 million loan and USD 5.29 million grant · effective 5 March 2026 · project value $54.2 million
register.text: Lends through La Banque Agricole so that farmers can invest in climate-smart practices along agricultural value chains. The Green Climate Fund expects about 687,000 people to gain greater resilience.

register.name: Institutional Support Project for Domestic Resource Mobilisation and Investment Attractiveness (PAIMRAI), phase 2
register.detail: Approved 17 July 2026 · more than UA 26 million
register.text: Supports the modernisation of tax administration, public debt management and public spending, and the reforms that follow the Court of Audit’s review of public finances from 2019 to March 2024. It also backs small businesses and young and women entrepreneurs.

register.name: ITFC annual financing plan 2026
register.detail: Signed, release of 11 February 2026 · imports and exports of essential commodities
register.text: Trade finance for imports and exports of essential commodities, mainly petroleum products and groundnuts, for energy and food security. ITFC has approved US$2.8 billion for Senegal since 2008.

register.name: IFC and Société Générale Sénégal
register.detail: Release of 13 March 2026 · senior loan, about XOF 32.8 billion · IDA Private Sector Window
register.note: At least 10% for women-owned or women-led businesses
register.text: A five-year expansion of lending to micro, small and medium enterprises, including in health, education and renewable energy. IFC estimates it will help create 12,000 to 21,000 indirect jobs.

register.name: BIDC-EBID credit line to BNDE
register.note: Reserved for financing small and medium enterprises
register.text: A new credit line from the ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development to the Banque Nationale pour le Développement Economique, reserved for lending to small and medium enterprises in Senegal.
by: ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development
Banque Nationale pour le Développement Economique

register.name: IFC and EDK Group
register.detail: Release of 19 December 2025 · mostly in local currency (XOF 16.4 billion) · IDA Private Sector Window
register.note: Up to 18 new grocery stores by 2027
register.text: Finances the renovation of EDK’s Low Price stores and up to 18 new grocery outlets by 2027, mainly in lower-income towns outside Dakar such as Fatick and Kaolack. About 2,450 direct and indirect jobs are expected.

register.name: IFC and Carrefour Médical
register.detail: Release of 4 December 2025 · long-term, mostly local currency (XOF 12 billion) · IDA Private Sector Window
register.note: Medical equipment and dialysis consumables made in Senegal
register.text: Long-term finance for a Senegalese supplier of medical equipment and consumables that also runs a dialysis consumables production unit. It supports local supply to hospitals in Senegal and the region.

register.name: IFC and Banque Islamique du Sénégal
register.detail: Release of 7 October 2025 · Islamic financing · IDA Private Sector Window
register.note: IFC’s first Islamic financing in sub-Saharan Africa
register.text: Islamic finance for micro, small and medium enterprises, including women-led firms, through the first fully Islamic bank in the West African Economic and Monetary Union. The bank aims to nearly triple its lending to such firms, to about $350 million over five years.

register.name: EIB and La Banque Agricole
register.detail: Signed 30 August 2024 · with European Union support
register.note: At least 30% for climate action and 30% for women
register.text: Finances production investment by more than 3,000 agricultural workers in cereals, horticulture, groundnuts and cashews, including irrigation, mechanisation and storage. It lends to the farms behind the food standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 56 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A colourful street in Dakar, Senegal

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Groundnut and millet fields in the Senegalese countryside under a wide sky

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Baobab trees and dry savanna woodland in Senegal

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Enough to supply every home, once it is stored, treated and piped.
items.alt: The Senegal River at Saint-Louis with painted pirogues

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of electricity from renewables, 2023
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: Wind turbines of the Taiba Ndiaye wind farm in Senegal

items.name: EDK Group
items.text: A Senegalese grocery retailer whose Low Price stores sell food beyond Dakar. With IFC finance it plans up to 18 new outlets by 2027, mainly in lower-income towns such as Fatick and Kaolack.

items.name: SEN’EAU (SUEZ)
items.text: Runs urban drinking water services in partnership with the State, with continuous access to quality water for 10 million people. It has made about 200,000 cubic metres more a day available to Dakar residents.

items.name: Kael and Kahone solar plants (Engie, Meridiam, FONSIS)
items.text: Two solar plants of 60 MWac in all, built under the World Bank Group’s Scaling Solar programme and commissioned in 2021. They supply nearly 540,000 people at under 4 euro cents a kilowatt-hour.

items.name: Carrefour Médical
items.text: Supplies medical equipment and consumables to hospitals in Senegal and the region, delivers complete health facility projects and runs a dialysis consumables production unit.

items.name: Banque Islamique du Sénégal
items.text: The first fully Islamic bank in the West African Economic and Monetary Union, lending to micro, small and medium enterprises, including women-led firms. It aims to nearly triple that lending, to about $350 million over five years.
